$comment: This file is DATA, not code. Every entry here exists because a real
false negative was observed against live supplier data. The system is
meant to improve by growing this file, not by growing if-statements —
nothing in src/ names a product.
Abbreviations expand BEFORE containers are stripped, which is why 'BTL'
disappears from the query (it becomes BOTTLE, then a container) while
'LOZ' survives as LOZENGES (a product form, not a container).
$comment_synonyms: Phrase-level equivalences applied to EVERY product, longest phrase first.
The VALUE is the canonical form both sides collapse to. Two rules keep this
safe and they are enforced at load time:
1. A value must not contain its own key as a whole word. 'zero' ->
'zero sugar' would re-match itself and grow without limit.
2. A value should be a form that is not itself a key, or the two rewrites
chain in an order that depends on phrase length rather than intent.
Prefer contracting to a single token ('no added sugar' -> 'nosugar') over
expanding: single tokens cannot re-trigger a multi-word key.
$comment_brandSynonyms: Commercial wording that is equivalent ONLY within one brand's range.
Scoped because these equivalences are not universally true: 'Zero' means
'Zero Sugar' on Coca-Cola, but on another range Zero could be a distinct
product. A brand's map applies only when its key appears as whole words in
the text, so nothing leaks between ranges.
COCA COLA ZERO BOTTLE          <-> Coca-Cola Zero Sugar Bottle
PEPSI MAX NO ADDED SUGAR BOTTLE <-> Pepsi Max No Sugar Cola Bottle
TRUE variants must never appear here. White, Dark, Cherry, Vanilla, Diet
and Lemon distinguish real products and have to stay comparable.

pepsi.$comment: Only true equivalences. 'cola' was deleted here once — that
pepsi.$comment2: made one token mean different things in different products,
pepsi.$comment3: which the token-category invariant forbids. COLA is a brand
pepsi.$comment4: token in Coca-Cola and a product descriptor in Pepsi Cola;
pepsi.$comment5: it is never noise, and is never deleted.

$comment_retailNoise: Retailer-only decorations. These say how the LINE is ordered, not what
the product is, so they are removed from the query and kept in metadata.
$comment_retailNoise2: CATALOGUE NOISE ONLY. Packaging quantities (case, each, single, outer,
inner) were removed from this list — they are `packaging`, and a token
cannot hold two categories. They are still stripped from the identity, just
under the category that actually describes them.
retailNoise: $note: PRICE MARKING. A price-marked pack is the same commercial product
$note: as an unmarked one — the marking says how the LINE is priced, never
$note: what the product is. These are what let two listings of one product
$note: collapse to a single commercial identity instead of looking like a
$note: choice the buyer has to make.
$comment_productForms: Physical product form. Extracted to metadata and removed from the canonical
identity, then compared as its OWN attribute — exactly like a container.
WRIGLEYS EXTRA PEPPERMINT GUM 46P -> WRIGLEYS EXTRA PEPPERMINT
Both sides are normalized the same way, so a retailer writing GUM and a
supplier omitting it still agree. Removing it from the TEXT stops it being
compared twice, and keeps it out of the supplier search box where the
tracer proved extra tokens suppress results.
FLAVOURS ARE NOT FORMS. 'mint' and 'cherry' distinguish real products and

$comment_pieceCountPatterns: Piece / unit counts a retailer appends: '46P', '10 PCE', '20 PIECES'.
Pure retail metadata. The tracer proved '46P' suppresses the supplier
search entirely — dropping it from the canonical is what makes the product
findable, and the count is preserved in metadata.
$comment_abvPatterns: SAFETY-CRITICAL. An ABV of 0.0 marks an alcohol-free product, which is a
DIFFERENT commercial product from the same brand at full strength:
GUINNESS DRAUGHT 0.0% CAN 4 PCK  <->  Guinness Draught 0.0% Can 4 Pack
NOT  Guinness Draught Stout Can 4 Pack
Extracted as a percentage — a structural pattern, not a product word — and
an ABV of 0 becomes the 'alcoholfree' variant so it is compared as a
variant and can never match a full-strength listing. Leaving '0.0%' as
loose text put a bare number in the identity AND in the search box.
$comment_multipackPatterns: A multipack IS commercially meaningful — a 10-pack is not a single — but it
is a QUANTITY, not part of the product's name. Like the pack size, it is
extracted to metadata and compared as its own attribute, so it never sits
in the search box or the identity comparison.
Runs AFTER abbreviations, so '10PK' has already become '10 PACK'.
$comment_countableNoise: Packaging nouns that are noise ON THEIR OWN but meaningful when counted.
HALLS SOOTHERS CHERRY PACK   'pack' is packaging -> removed
SMARTIES HEXATUBE 4 PACK     '4 pack' is a multipack -> kept
Stripping these unconditionally would erase multipack counts, which are the
signal that separates a single from a 4-pack. Stripped only when NOT
$comment_containers: Physical packaging. Removed from the query and kept in metadata, because
the rule engine already compares containers as their own attribute — a
container word left in the text would be counted twice.
$comment_decorations: Supplier catalogue decoration — words a supplier's own catalogue style
adds that carry no commercial identity. '*' applies to every supplier;
named keys apply only to that supplier.
Every entry below was verified against a real pair of listings that are
Nestle Smarties Hexatube   <-> Nestle Std Smarties Hexatube   (std)
Mentos Mint Roll           <-> Mentos Chewy Mint Roll         (chewy)
Halls Extra Strong         <-> Halls Extra Strong Menthol Action Sweets
CAUTION: entries here are asserted to be commercially meaningless. A word
that actually distinguishes two products must NOT be added — that would
merge them. 'menthol' is included only because Halls Extra Strong IS the
menthol product; remove it if a range appears where menthol is a variant.

*: $note: A token's category is a property of the TOKEN, not of the product
$note: it appears in. These were previously here and have been removed
$note: because they are PRODUCT DESCRIPTORS in every product that has
$note:   chocolate hazelnut spread bread sticks dip wafers biscuits
$note: Deleting identity words to force a match is unfalsifiable — any
$note: bad match can be 'fixed' that way, and the dictionary grows
$note: forever. Extra descriptors are handled by field comparison.

$comment_pricePatterns: Shelf and promotional prices embedded in retailer descriptions. Captured
into metadata rather than discarded — a shelf price is real information
